title: Tenant-aware cluster access matrix with SLA strip and upgrade-impact heatmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design ticket to prototype and validate a tenant-aware Cluster Access Matrix panel for the Private/VPC Console. The panel combines three coordinated widgets: (1) an access matrix that surfaces which tenants and teams can reach each private cluster and which network paths are permitted, (2) an SLA strip that shows per-cluster SLOs (latency/availability) and current burn rate, and (3) an upgrade-impact heatmap that predicts tenant exposure for scheduled upgrades and maintenance windows. Goal: give platform owners and SREs a single view to make rollout decisions, surface cross-tenant risk, and tie in cost attribution for reserved capacity impacts.
acceptance_criteria: Design mockups for desktop and tablet breakpoints for the cluster panel (desktop primary)
Interactive Figma prototype demonstrating hover details for SLA strip and heatmap cell drilldowns
Content and label review with Product and Security (access labels and role filters validated)
Performance target: console should render panel for >= 200 clusters in under 400ms (client-side virtualized list)
Design tokens and spacing follow redeployed console system — deliver React-ready spec and CSS vars
Accessibility: contrast, keyboard nav, and screen reader labels verified for all interactive cells
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created with concept sketches. Key challenge: how to avoid exposing tenant names to non-authorized users while still surfacing aggregate risk. Proposed approach: obfuscate tenant IDs and require hover-to-reveal for users with 'view-tenant-details' permission.

2025-02-12 Marco Jensen: First pass layout attached in Figma. Decided to place SLA strip above the matrix so engineers can scan SLO statuses quickly. Added small sparkline to each SLA cell to show 24h trend.

2025-02-13 Priya Nair (PM): Request to add cost-attribution column that shows estimated monthly reserved-cost impact per tenant when cluster is in 'reserved' vs 'burst' mode. See PM-233 for alignment.

2025-02-14 Security review (Oliver Wang): Raised concern about exposing network CIDR notes in hover cards. Decision: hide full CIDRs, show abstracted path like 'VPC-peering: partner-A (restricted)'. Security also requested an audit-log link in the drilldown panel.

2025-02-15 Eng sync (ENG-19821): Engineering flagged backend data model gaps — need tenant->cluster membership and scheduled maintenance projection API (ETA: ENG-21235). Workaround: prototype with static dataset and simulated schedules.
2025-02-16 Design critique: Feedback from Console UX team — heatmap colors too saturated for users with deuteranopia. Updated palette and added pattern overlay option for high-risk cells.

2025-02-17 Marco Jensen: Prototype updated to include 'canary-safe' toggle that filters matrix rows to only show clusters with canary routing enabled. This is to support canary-aware rollouts from the Console.
2025-02-18 Aisha Patel: Submitting for formal design review. Attached expected edge-cases doc and proposed microcopy for SLA states (Healthy / Degraded / At-risk / Outage).
decisions: Obfuscate tenant identifiers for non-privileged viewers; full tenant name revealed only to users with 'view-tenant-details' scope
SLA strip is persistent at the top of the cluster panel and condenses to a glyph in compact view
Heatmap uses three visual channels: color (risk), pattern overlay (colorblind safe), and numeric badge for exposed-tenants count
Cost-attribution column will display estimated monthly delta and link to Cost Explorer; precise billing numbers require backend mapping (ENG-21235)
Prototype will use virtualized rows client-side to meet the render performance target
tradeoffs: Showing tenant names improves actionable context for SREs but increases surface area for data exposure; we mitigate with role gating and obfuscation
Including cost numbers in the matrix provides decision context but requires backend joins that may add latency — will implement asynchronous enrichment with optimistic UI
Detailed CIDR information is valuable in debugging but conflicts with least-privilege constraints; prefer linked drilldown to audit logs instead
next_steps: Design: finalize Figma frames for mobile/tablet and add interaction states (hover, focus, keyboard) — due 2025-02-21
Eng: prioritise ENG-21235 (tenant->cluster mapping & maintenance projection API) for prototype parity — eng lead assigned
PM: validate with two early customers (regulated fintech and mid-market SaaS) for feedback on obfuscation model — outreach in progress
Security: schedule a focused review on microcopy and audit-link flows before implementation kickoff
Follow-up: create a lightweight A/B experiment plan to test 'SLA strip upfront' vs 'SLA in detail pane' in 10% of accounts post-release
